title: A Full Skin Defect Model to Evaluate Vascularization of Biomaterials In Vivo
protocol: Generate samples of scaffolds using 12 mm biopsy punches.
Drain scaffolds by gently squeezing them with sterile gauze.
Rehydrate scaffolds by adding 160 µl of a solution containing bioactive molecules or cells.
Check success of bioactivation with cells through metabolic assays such as MTT Assays.
Fix compounds or cells to be tested inside the scaffold by delivering them in a fibrin-thrombin solution or hydrogel, again through rehydration.
Cut out round pieces of titanized meshes approximately 14 mm in diameter for each experiment and control group.
Choose the animal and strain carefully.
Shave the back of furred animals before implantation of scaffolds.
Use mice aged 6 to 8 weeks with a body weight between 20 g and 25 g.
Conduct the operation under sterile conditions.
Maintain the animal’s normal body temperature using a warming mat.
Administer Buprenorphin at a dose of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously every 8 hours before anesthesia.
Place the animal under inhalative anesthesia (Isoflurane) or use equivalent standard procedures.
Confirm anesthesia by gently squeezing the animal’s toes or through a skin pinch.
Inject 0.5 ml physiologic saline solution subcutaneously at the beginning of the operation to prevent exsiccosis.
Place the animal in a prone position and mark the midline of the mouse's back with a fine tip permanent pen.
Define the excision area for the skin defects as shown.
Ensure that defects are not placed too caudally to avoid animals removing dressings and scaffolds.
Create round bilateral defects using a 10 mm biopsy punch.
Carefully delineate the excision area without cutting completely through the skin.
Gently lift off the marked skin with forceps.
Incise along the marked circle using fine surgical scissors.
In case of bleeding, carefully compress with sterile gauze.
Extend the separation of skin and underlying tissue at the wound borders for 2-4 mm.
Place the titanized mesh into the defect directly on the wound bed.
Place scaffolds directly over the mesh.
Suture the scaffolds to the adjacent wound edges with 4 to 6 single knots.
Suture a transparent wound dressing above the defects to protect the scaffold.
Evaluate the general state of the animal daily by observing motor activity, body weight, signs of pain, tolerance to the dressing and auto-mutilation.
Monitor the wound area for bleeding, local and systemic signs of infection and the position of the dressing.
Inject Buprenorphin daily at a dose of 0.05-0.1 mg/kg bodyweight or equivalent analgesic medication.
Replace or reattach the wound dressing under anesthesia if the mouse removes or damages it.
Sacrifice animals by overdoses of Pentobarbital (150 mg/kg) at desired time points.
Mark the site of skin excision with a permanent marker, including scaffolds and as much of the mouse back skin as possible.
Incise the skin along marked lines with scissors or a scalpel.
Detach the entire skin, including scaffolds and titanized mesh, from underlying tissue through blunt preparation.
Place the explanted tissue stretched out on a Petri dish.
Set up a transillumination device by mounting a Petri dish above a strong source of white light (100 Watt standard light bulb).
Fix a digital camera above the transilluminator to obtain digital pictures.
Place samples upside down on the Petri dish over the transillumination device.
Take pictures of the complete scaffolds in macro mode.
Take pictures of equally sized areas of normal skin.
Store the images in TIFF format for further digital analysis.
Save the tissue for further biochemical or histological analysis.
Download and install VesSeg-Tool software.
Open the picture with VesSeg-Tool software.
Select the area of the image covered by the scaffold for digital analysis.
Use the option “Hysteresis thresholding” to increase the contrast of vessels (Image→Vessel enhancement filter→Hysteresis thresholding→Top-Hat transformation→Calculate vessel enhancement).
Proceed with the segmentation of the vessel map (Image→Vessel enhancement filter→Hysteresis thresholding→Threshold borders).
Select the first threshold (“Vessel coverage”) to label every pixel that is even remotely vessel-like as a vessel.
Select the second threshold (“Background coverage”) to label only those pixels that are particularly vessel-like as vessels.
Check the automatic segmentation proposal manually to add non-captured vessels and eliminate common false-positive structures such as hairs or sutures.
Calculate the length of the vessels using image analysis software.
Determine the overall area covered by vessels using binary image statistics.
Thin the vessels in the resulting vessel map to lines with a width of one pixel.
Analyze the native skin area under the same parameters as the scaffolds.
Assign a value of 100% to the native tissue for comparison purposes.
Relate the scaffold's vascularization percentage to that of the native tissue.
Adjust the number of white pixels coverage considering the difference in areas between a circle and a square.
